topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, outlines the interdisciplinary audience, and presents the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Multistep Disruption of Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cumulative genetic and epigenetic alterations disrupt normal developmental differentiation programs and tissue architecture to initiate malignancy.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Models of Tumor Invasion and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from benign to invasive and metastatic states, using histological criteria and colorectal cancer as a stepwise model.

topics.label: Principles of Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic defines the systematic naming conventions and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant neoplasms based on tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the anatomical, metabolic, and metastatic processes by which primary and secondary tumors cause illness and patient death.

topics.label: Comparative Tumor Incidence Across Tissues and Animal Taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the frequency and mortality of different tumor types in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Presentation and Cancer Screening Modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the clinical signs of cancer and assess the utility, histological targets, and limitations of population screening across various organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Session Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by reiterating the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping directions for upcoming practicals.
